social_history.living_situation: Lives with husband and 2 young children

patient.chief_complaint: Unusual behavior, severe insomnia, and 'not being herself' for 10 days, brought in by husband
patient.history_present_illness: A 30-year-old right-handed Hispanic woman was brought to the emergency department by her husband who reports that over the past 10 days she has undergone a dramatic personality change that he describes as completely out of character. She is a school teacher and was in her normal state of health until approximately 12 days ago when she began complaining of difficulty sleeping, restlessness, and feeling 'on edge.' Over the subsequent days she became increasingly fearful that someone was watching the family home and began insisting her husband lock all the windows and doors at specific times. She refused to allow the children to go to school, stating she 'had a feeling something bad would happen.' Her speech became progressively more fragmented and she began having long periods of staring blankly at the wall, unresponsive to her husband calling her name. He took her to their primary care physician five days ago who attributed the symptoms to anxiety and postpartum-equivalent stress and prescribed lorazepam 0.5 mg. The lorazepam provided minimal benefit and she continued to deteriorate. She has not slept more than 1-2 hours per night for the past week. On the day of presentation she had an episode where she appeared to be chewing and making repetitive lip movements for about 30 seconds, after which she was confused for several minutes. This alarmed her husband who brought her to the ED. She has a history of migraines but her husband states this presentation is entirely unlike any migraine she has had before. She had a mild cold with low-grade fever approximately 3 weeks ago that lasted about one week. No recent travel. Last menstrual period was 3 weeks ago; she is not pregnant.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert but confused. Oriented to person only. Responds to simple commands inconsistently. Speech is fragmented with word-finding difficulty. Intermittent periods of blank staring lasting 15-30 seconds with unresponsiveness. Periodic lip-smacking and oromandibular automatisms observed during examination.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils 3mm, equal, reactive. Extraocular movements intact without nystagmus. Mild facial asymmetry with right lower facial droop (new per husband). Tongue midline.
neurological_exam.motor: Mild bilateral upper extremity tremor at rest. Tone mildly increased bilaterally. Full strength 5/5 in all extremities on manual testing.
neurological_exam.sensory: Grossly intact to light touch. Limited cooperation for detailed sensory exam.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-nose slightly dysmetric bilaterally; may be due to tremor.
neurological_exam.gait: Wide-based, cautious gait. No ataxia on tandem.
neurological_exam.additional: No nuchal rigidity. Mild tachycardia and blood pressure lability noted. Intermittent mild diaphoresis.

differential.key_features: Temporal lobe FLAIR signal, orofacial automatisms, recent viral prodrome — but HSV PCR negative, anti-NMDAR positive
Known migraine history — but acute personality change, orofacial automatisms, and seizures are not typical migraine features
Prescribed lorazepam — but clinical deterioration preceded lorazepam, and presentation not consistent with benzo toxicity
Anxiety-like presentation at onset — but rapid progression to automatisms and seizure-like episodes indicates organic pathology

optimal_actions.action: Pelvic ultrasound and CT body for teratoma workup

critical_actions: Continuous EEG monitoring mandatory — extreme delta brush may not be seen on short routine recording
Anti-NMDAR antibody testing in serum and CSF is diagnostic
Pelvic imaging required — teratoma identified and must be resected
Do not attribute orofacial automatisms solely to anxiety or benzodiazepine effect
contraindicated_actions: Attributing orofacial automatisms to medication side effects without EEG evaluation
Using lorazepam as primary treatment for what are likely subclinical seizures from autoimmune encephalitis
Diagnosing migraine-related episode without pursuing organic encephalitis workup
Failing to send anti-NMDAR antibodies despite orofacial automatisms and psychiatric symptoms in young woman
key_reasoning_points: Orofacial dyskinesias and automatisms in a young woman with behavioral change should prompt immediate consideration of anti-NMDAR encephalitis
The subtle unilateral temporal FLAIR signal could be artifact or early disease — the key diagnostic step is anti-NMDAR antibody testing, not MRI alone
Extreme delta brush pattern on continuous EEG is pathognomonic for anti-NMDAR encephalitis — this would not appear on a 30-minute routine EEG
History of migraine is a red herring in this case — the presentation is entirely unlike typical migraine
Lorazepam prescribed by PCP may provide some temporary symptom reduction but does not treat the underlying autoimmune process

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The presentation of paranoia, personality change, orofacial automatisms, and sleep disturbance is not consistent with any migraine variant
